'''Marta Dark McNeese''' is an American physicist and professor at [[Spelman College]]. She was the first African American woman to receive a bachelor's degree in physics from the [[University of Virginia]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Roberson |first=Stephen |date=21 February 2020 |title=The National Society of Black Physicists honors Dr. Marta Dark McNeese. Dr. McNeese is a professor of physics at Spelman College. She endeavors to be a mentor to other young women interested in a STEM career, particularly in physics |url=https://nsbp.org/blogpost/1904681/362817/February-21-2020 |access-date=20 March 2023 |website=[[National Society of Black Physicists]]}}</ref> Her research focuses on laser interactions with biological tissues and electro-optical effects in biomolecules, and has applications in light-emitting devices, diodes for displays, and flexible light-emitting materials.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=SPEAKERS |url=https://cuwip.ua.edu/speakers.html |access-date=2023-03-22 |website=Conference for UG Women in Physics |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Marta Dark McNeese |url=http://www.aps.org/careers/physicists/profiles/mcneese.cfm |access-date=2023-03-23 |website=www.aps.org |language=en}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
McNeese grew up in [[Prince George's County, Maryland]]. She attended [[Eleanor Roosevelt High School (Maryland)|Eleanor Roosevelt High School]] in [[Greenbelt, Maryland]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Speakers and Panelists |url=https://sciences.ucf.edu/physics/scuwp/speakers-and-panelists/ |access-date=2023-03-22 |website=Southeast Conference for Undergraduate Women in Physics at UCF |language=en-US}}</ref> Her high school had a focus on science and math programming.<ref name=":3" />

She attended the [[University of Virginia]] in [[Charlottesville, Virginia]], for her undergraduate studies. There, she started in the College of Engineering, but switched to the College of Arts and Sciences in her first year. She majored in physics and minored in astrophysics and studied with [[Bascom S. Deaver]] and [[Lou Bloomfield]], graduating in 1992. She was a volunteer DJ at the [[University of Virginia]] while she was a student. During her undergraduate studies, she completed an undergraduate research experience at [[Lehigh University]] and interned at [[IBM]] for a summer.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last=Physics |first=American Institute of |date=2021-09-24 |title=Marta Dark McNeese |url=https://www.aip.org/history-programs/niels-bohr-library/oral-histories/45108 |access-date=2023-03-22 |website=www.aip.org |language=en}}</ref>

McNeese went on to attended the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] for her doctoral studies. Her thesis was titled "The physical response of soft musculoskeletal tissues to short pulsed laser irradiation," and her doctoral advisor was [[Michael Stephen Feld]].<ref>{{Cite thesis |title=The physical response of soft musculoskeletal tissues to short pulsed laser irradiation |url=https://dspace.mit.edu/handle/1721.1/9538 |publisher=Massachusetts Institute of Technology |date=1999 |degree=Thesis |first=Marta Lyselle |last=Dark|hdl=1721.1/9538 }}</ref> At MIT, she was part of the Spectroscopy Lab,<ref>{{Cite web |title=MIT Spectroscopy Lab - People - Faculty |url=https://web.mit.edu/spectroscopy/people/alumni.html |access-date=2023-03-23 |website=web.mit.edu}}</ref> worked in the Laser Biomedical Research Center, and was a teacher's assistant for an introductory physics course.<ref name=":1" />

== Career ==
After completing her PhD, McNeese stayed on at MIT as a postdoc for two months before accepting a postdoctoral position at the [[United States Naval Research Laboratory]] in Washington, D.C. After about a year at the [[United States Naval Research Laboratory|Naval Research Laboratory]], McNeese was hired as a faculty member at [[Spelman College]] in [[Atlanta|Atlanta, Georgia]], in 2000.<ref name=":2" />

At this point, Spelman's physics program was in its early stages, and at the time of McNeese's hiring, the department grew from three to five faculty members. The effort to establish a physics program at Spelman was led by [[Etta Zuber Falconer]] at the time. McNeese specifically helped develop a biophysics course at the college at the beginning of her tenure.

She is a member of numerous professional groups, including [[Optica (society)|Optica]] and the [[American Association of Physics Teachers]], and also serves on the latter's committee on diversity, committee on women, and editorial board for ''The Physics Teachers''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Physics Teacher |url=https://aapt.scitation.org/pte/info/board?doi=10.1119/pte |access-date=2023-03-20 |website=The Physics Teacher | doi=<!-- --> |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":4" /> She is a member of the [[American Physical Society]] and has served on the group's Committee on Minorities, Panel on Public Affairs, and is currently a General Councilor.<ref name=":0" /> As a member of the [[National Society of Black Physicists]], she has co-chaired the group's Chemical and Biological Physics section.<ref name=":1" />

McNeese is currently associate professor of physics and Chair of the physics department at [[Spelman College]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Marta Dark McNeese |url=https://www.spelman.edu/academics/majors-and-programs/physics/faculty/marta-dark-mcneese |access-date=2023-03-22 |website=www.spelman.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=U.S. Black colleges train an outsize share of physics majors—but they can't do it all |url=https://www.science.org/content/article/u-s-black-colleges-train-outsize-share-physics-majors-they-can-t-do-it-all |access-date=2023-03-23 |website=www.science.org |language=en}}</ref>
